findings.body: The UI and query schema advertise SQL expressions as available, but every corresponding backend request is rejected, leaving enabled installations with a selectable capability that cannot execute.
findings.failure_mode: Clients construct and submit requests for an advertised feature that the server unconditionally rejects.
findings.impact: The UI and query schema advertise SQL expressions as available, but every corresponding backend request is rejected, leaving enabled installations with a selectable capability that cannot execute.
findings.root_cause: The backend was hard-disabled without removing the externally visible feature flag and query-type advertisements that indicate the capability is available.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep backend execution disabled, but retire or force-disable `sqlExpressions` in the configuration exposed to the frontend and remove SQL from the advertised query-type schema until a safe implementation exists.
findings.title: Retained feature flag still advertises a backend-disabled SQL capability
findings.trigger: An administrator enables `sqlExpressions`; the frontend checks that same configured flag to expose SQL expressions, or an API client discovers the still-advertised SQL query type and submits one through `ExpressionQueryReader`.
findings.verifier_reason: The patch adds enableSqlExpressions() at lines 194-200 which always returns false regardless of the flag value (both branches return false). The feature flag FlagSqlExpressions still exists in toggles_gen.go:584 and documentation at index.md:187 advertises it as enabling SQL expressions. The frontend check at public/app/features/expressions/types.ts:73 uses config.featureToggles?.sqlExpressions, so enabling the flag would expose the UI option while backend unconditionally rejects with 'sqlExpressions is not implemented'. This is a real API contract mismatch.

pr.body:
<!--

Thank you for sending a pull request! Here are some tips:

1. If this is your first time, please read our contribution guide at https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

2. Ensure you include and run the appropriate tests as part of your Pull Request.

3. In a new feature or configuration option, an update to the documentation is necessary. Everything related to the documentation is under the docs folder in the root of the repository.

4. If the Pull Request is a work in progress, make use of GitHub's "Draft PR" feature and mark it as such.

5. If you can not merge your Pull Request due to a merge conflict, Rebase it. This gets it in sync with the main branch.

6. Name your PR as "<FeatureArea>: Describe your change", e.g. Alerting: Prevent race condition. If it's a fix or feature relevant for the changelog describe the user impact in the title. The PR title is used to auto-generate the changelog for issues marked with the "add to changelog" label.

7. If your PR content should be added to the What's New document for the next major or minor release, add the **add to what's new** label to your PR. Note that you should add this label to the main PR that introduces the feature; do not add this label to smaller PRs for the feature.

-->

**What is this feature?**

Remove reference to DuckDB

**Why do we need this feature?**

See the blog post describing the vulnerability, for which a fix was rolled out to all Grafana versions earlier today:
https://grafana.com/blog/2024/10/17/grafana-security-release-critical-severity-fix-for-cve-2024-9264/

The full extent of our documentation around this feature seems to be here:
https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/81666/files#diff-16fb71b28e5b6197615abba8a07bc73d9bf75ebc60311663e1c29976de5cc9a6

All we've documented is that the feature-flag exists. That flag still exists in the codebase, so I'm tempted not to touch that documentation for now. We can always follow up with more improvements after this PR.

**Who is this feature for?**

Everyone

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

This moves the security fix into Grafana repo itself, now that it has been publicly announced. We need this here so we can clean up and simplify our Security-releases pipeline once again.

**Special notes for your reviewer:**

Please check that:
- [x] It works as expected from a user's perspective.
   Behaviour of this patch was already verified manually by @toddtreece. See his confirmation of this on our private slack, [here](https://raintank-corp.slack.com/archives/C07P60RBAUD/p1727902629844259?thread_ts=1727901896.911799&cid=C07P60RBAUD)
   Tested again on the Ephemeral instance here: https://ephemeral1511182194942samjewe.grafana-dev.net/d/be18gem24w2dcf/test-sql-expressions-bugfix?from=now-1h&to=now&timezone=browser
- [ ] If this is a pre-GA feature, it is behind a feature toggle.
- [ ] The docs are updated, and if this is a [notable improvement](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/contribute/release-notes/#how-to-determine-if-content-belongs-in-whats-new), it's added to our [What's New](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/contribute/release-notes/) doc.
pr.title: ServerSideExpressions: Disable SQL Expressions to prevent RCE and LFI vulnerability

raw_findings.body: The UI and query schema advertise SQL expressions as available, but every corresponding backend request is rejected, leaving enabled installations with a selectable capability that cannot execute.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Clients construct and submit requests for an advertised feature that the server unconditionally rejects.
raw_findings.impact: The UI and query schema advertise SQL expressions as available, but every corresponding backend request is rejected, leaving enabled installations with a selectable capability that cannot execute.
raw_findings.root_cause: The backend was hard-disabled without removing the externally visible feature flag and query-type advertisements that indicate the capability is available.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Keep backend execution disabled, but retire or force-disable `sqlExpressions` in the configuration exposed to the frontend and remove SQL from the advertised query-type schema until a safe implementation exists.
raw_findings.title: Retained feature flag still advertises a backend-disabled SQL capability
raw_findings.trigger: An administrator enables `sqlExpressions`; the frontend checks that same configured flag to expose SQL expressions, or an API client discovers the still-advertised SQL query type and submits one through `ExpressionQueryReader`.

raw_findings.body: The documentation states that the toggle enables SQL and DuckDB expressions even though the patched backend always disables them and removes the DuckDB implementation, causing users to configure an unsupported feature.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Documentation gives operators a configuration contract that no longer matches server behavior.
raw_findings.impact: The documentation states that the toggle enables SQL and DuckDB expressions even though the patched backend always disables them and removes the DuckDB implementation, causing users to configure an unsupported feature.
raw_findings.root_cause: The implementation and dependency were removed without updating the public and generated descriptions of the affected feature toggle.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Update the feature-toggle registry description and `docs/sources/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/feature-toggles/index.md` to state that SQL expressions are disabled or remove the toggle from published documentation; regenerate derived toggle files as required.
raw_findings.title: Update documentation that still claims the toggle enables SQL and DuckDB
raw_findings.trigger: A user consults the feature-toggle documentation or generated toggle description before enabling `sqlExpressions`.

raw_findings.body: There is no active test proving that SQL expressions remain rejected with `sqlExpressions` both enabled and disabled and with `expressionParser` both enabled and disabled; the existing SQL parser and command tests are skipped, so an accidental re-enable or path-specific bypass can pass CI.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Automated review cannot detect a regression that restores SQL execution or leaves one parser path behaving differently.
raw_findings.impact: There is no active test proving that SQL expressions remain rejected with `sqlExpressions` both enabled and disabled and with `expressionParser` both enabled and disabled; the existing SQL parser and command tests are skipped, so an accidental re-enable or path-specific bypass can pass CI.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch introduces a security gate and replaces execution with stubs without adding executable tests for the affected entry points and toggle combinations.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add table-driven tests covering both values of `FlagSqlExpressions` and `FlagExpressionParser`, asserting that SQL queries are rejected with a controlled error and that no SQL command reaches execution.
raw_findings.title: Add regression coverage for every SQL-expression parsing path
raw_findings.trigger: CI runs this security-sensitive change, or a later refactor modifies either the typed expression reader, the legacy `buildCMDNode` path, or the inert database stubs.

raw_findings.body: The negated toggle lookup and branch imply flag-dependent behavior even though both branches return false, obscuring whether the hard-disable is intentional or an inversion mistake and making future edits error-prone.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The code communicates a nonexistent dependency on the feature flag and reduces the reliability of review and maintenance of a security boundary.
raw_findings.impact: The negated toggle lookup and branch imply flag-dependent behavior even though both branches return false, obscuring whether the hard-disable is intentional or an inversion mistake and making future edits error-prone.
raw_findings.root_cause: The hard-disable was encoded as a redundant conditional whose outcomes are identical.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Replace the function body with an unconditional `return false` and a comment documenting why SQL expressions must remain disabled, or remove the helper and reject SQL directly.
raw_findings.title: Replace the dead feature-toggle branch with an explicit hard-disable
raw_findings.trigger: A reviewer or maintainer inspects or modifies the SQL-expression security gate.
